paragraphs: Mentioned in an aggadic passage in [Sanhedrin 108a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.108a.22) (Hyman cites 101a). In [Pesikta de-Rav Kahana](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesikta_DeRav_Kahana.17.6), at the printed locator קלב. (132), he disagrees with Resh Lakish. [Eikhah Rabbah 4:18](https://www.sefaria.org/Eikhah_Rabbah.4.18) reads Rabbi Afi of Caesarea; this is what Seder HaDorot means.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The notice has the form אפי, Afi, and the contextual variant-reading formula גרם. The printed Pesikta locator קלב. is retained without establishing its edition or page-versus-folio convention.

The linked Sanhedrin names Rabbi Yose of Caesarea in the discourse on Noah, and [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1962&lang=en) gives the same folio. In the parallel dispute about how the women colored their eyes, the linked Eikhah Rabbah names Rabbi Assi of Caesarea, while the linked Pesikta names Rabbi Nisa of Caesarea. Hyman reports Afi for Eikhah Rabbah. The digital Pesikta locator is 17:6. Hyman’s page 132 remains edition-dependent.
